contracts.commit_point: The lock-protected dedupe/append plus atomic_write_(self.path, rows) inside IntentStore.commit that durably writes committed-intents. (intent_store.py:47-56); all guards at intent_store.py:28-36 and dispatch_workflow.py:140-147 execute strictly before this point.
contracts.declared_mechanism: Fail-closed, layered validation before the write: (1) MaspAdapter.validate_intent deterministically rejects stale/unspecified world revisions and classifies risk — BLOCK_RESOURCE is R3_HIGH with approval_required=True and unknown resource IDs are error issues (engine_adapter.py:815-835, 895-922), REPORT_VEHICLE_FAULT/REQUEST_RECOVERY are R3_HIGH with approval_required=True (engine_adapter.py:923-936); the IntentValidation result is returned at engine_adapter.py:938-945. (2) DispatchWorkflowService.commit raises ValueError for invalid validation, raises PermissionError when an approval-required intent has no approval_id, and delegates to IntentStore.commit passing current_world_revision=engine.world_revision(scenario_id) (dispatch_workflow.py:140-153). (3) IntentStore.commit raises ValueError for non-simulation environment, stale world revision, non-APPROVED approval status, or approval/intent ID mismatch before any write, then performs a lock-protected, idempotent atomic write (intent_store.py:28-56). The API layer maps PermissionError->403 and ValueError->409 (api.py:960-965).
contracts.forbidden_condition: Durably persisting (committing) any of the following: (a) an intent that fails engine.validate_intent (ValueError, dispatch_workflow.py:140-142); (b) an intent whose environment != 'simulation' (ValueError, intent_store.py:28-29); (c) an intent whose basedOnWorldRevision != the current world revision (ValueError, intent_store.py:30-31); (d) an approval-required intent submitted without approval_id (PermissionError, dispatch_workflow.py:145-146); or (e) an approval-required intent whose supplied approval status is not APPROVED or whose approval.intent.intent_id does not match intent.intent_id (ValueError, intent_store.py:32-36).
pending_binding_information: AgentRunManager is constructed with workflow=dispatch_workflow (api.py:100-106), but agent_run_manager.py and orchestrator.py are not supplied, so no shown tool dispatch or agent run-loop invocation reaches DispatchWorkflowService.commit or IntentStore.commit; agent_mediation is therefore not_established.
orchestrator.tool_catalog() is exposed at GET /api/v1/agent/tools (api.py:588-590), but the catalog contents are not supplied; whether intent commit is registered as an agent tool is unknown.

Whether the configured agent runtime mode ('loop' or linear pipeline, settings.agent_runtime_mode wired at api.py:83) can generate DispatchIntents that flow into the commit endpoint or workflow.commit is not shown in the supplied source.

If agent mediation is later established, the applicable category (direct_tool vs agent_generated_input_to_guarded_effect) will depend on whether the agent invokes commit as a tool or supplies the intent body that an operator commits.
contracts.protected_operation: Committing a DispatchIntent to the committed-intents store via DispatchWorkflowService.commit (dispatch_workflow.py:133-160) which delegates to IntentStore.commit (intent_store.py:20-56), entered from POST /api/v1/intents/{intent_id}/commit (api.py:945-965).
contracts.protected_resource: The persistent committed-intents store at settings.data_dir / 'committed-intents.' (constructed at api.py:72), holding SIMULATION_COMMITTED records; per its class contract it 'stores simulation commitments only; it never writes to a field controller' (intent_store.py:12-13), and each record carries the notice that the commit writes only to the simulation environment (intent_store.py:45).
contracts.protection_obligation: A dispatch intent must not be durably committed to the committed-intents store unless it passes deterministic MASP validation, targets the 'simulation' environment, is bound to the current world revision of the target scenario, and — when deterministic validation classifies it high-risk (R3_HIGH with approvalRequired=true, e.g. BLOCK_RESOURCE, REPORT_VEHICLE_FAULT, REQUEST_RECOVERY) — carries an approval record whose status is APPROVED and whose intentId matches the intent. The guard chain is DispatchWorkflowService.commit -> IntentStore.commit, reachable via POST /api/v1/intents/{intent_id}/commit. (Merged duplicate phase-1/phase-2 reviewer wording; single obligation, single commit point.)
scope_limits: Simulation-only by construction: IntentStore records status 'SIMULATION_COMMITTED' with an explicit notice that no commands are sent to real vehicles (intent_store.py:37-46) and the class docstring states it never writes to a field controller (intent_store.py:13). No field/device or process effect is claimed or guarded by this contract.

Idempotent dedupe short-circuit: if a record with the same intentId already exists in the store, commit returns the existing record without appending (intent_store.py:51-53). The fail-closed guards still run first, but a previously committed intent is returned unchanged rather than re-validated against the new revision for record creation.

The APPROVED-status and intentId-match checks in IntentStore.commit execute only when approval is not None (intent_store.py:32-36); the requirement that approval-required intents supply an approval at all is enforced upstream by DispatchWorkflowService.commit raising PermissionError when approval_id is None (dispatch_workflow.py:144-147). DispatchWorkflowService.commit itself does not verify the fetched approval's identity; that match check lives only in IntentStore.commit:35-36.

engine_adapter.validate_intent treats basedOnWorldRevision == 0 as a warning ('unspecified'), not an error (engine_adapter.py:828-835); the strict equality requirement that binds the commit to the live revision is imposed at IntentStore.commit:30-31, not at validation time.

The Bearer-token middleware (api.py:177-192), CORSMiddleware registration (api.py:166-171), and server-side operator identity resolution on approval decisions (api.py:920-942) are ordinary web authentication/admission controls; they are not compiled as agent DEC contracts because no supplied source binds them to an agent tool, agent lifecycle hook, or agent-generated input reaching a guarded effect.

scenario_id is a caller-supplied query parameter on the commit route (api.py:949); the 'current world revision' the intent must match is derived from that scenario's file bytes plus the locked engine commit hash (engine_adapter.py:721-726), so revision binding is relative to the caller-chosen scenario.

command_center/contracts.py is not supplied: DispatchIntent field semantics (default of the environment field used at intent_store.py:28-29, intent_id generation, and aliasing of basedOnWorldRevision -> based_on_world_revision) cannot be verified from source.

command_center/approvals.py is not supplied: how an approval reaches ApprovalStatus.APPROVED is not shown; DispatchWorkflowService.decide_approval records an 'authenticated' flag in the audit payload (dispatch_workflow.py:119-130) but no supplied source shows enforcement requiring authenticated decisions, and api.py:229-232 discloses that approver identity is only trusted when an API token is configured.

command_center/auth.py is not supplied: is_protected / token_matches / operator_dependency implementations are unverifiable; the Bearer-token middleware (api.py:177-192) was not compiled as a contract because it is ordinary web authentication with no supplied agent binding.

command_center/storage.py is not supplied: the atomic_write_ implementation (used at intent_store.py:55) is unverifiable, so atomicity/durability semantics of the commit point are assumed from its name only.

command_center/settings.py is not supplied: the relationship between settings.app_env and the intent-level 'simulation' environment check (intent_store.py:28-29) is not established; the simulation-only claim in the obligation rests on the IntentStore guard, docstring, and record notice (intent_store.py:13, 28-29, 45) plus the advertised safety block (api.py:225-233), not on a settings-level enforcement shown in source.
Behavior labels and prevalence data are unavailable per the stated scope; nothing in this unit asserts how often the commit path is exercised by agents versus human operators.
